topic: Source integrity: five held files are not the works they claim to be
whyItMatters: An aggregator cover page carrying the correct title and ISBN, followed by unrelated text, is indistinguishable from a real copy in a file listing. Three of these were recorded as "genuine content after promotional pages", which would have allowed them to be cited.
currentSourceSignal: Audit on 2026-09-11 opened every file, hashed it, counted its pages and read its front matter. SRC-008, SRC-009, SRC-010, SRC-014 and SRC-015 carry 3-6% peptide-domain vocabulary across their pages, concentrated in the wrapper; their bodies are climate policy, Hume scholarship, fiction in three languages, African Union politics and project management. SRC-011 holds authentic Humana front matter and the opening of Chapter 1, then filler. SRC-013 is a two-page contents listing. SRC-001 to SRC-007 and SRC-012 are confirmed complete.
neededVerification: Obtain clean copies of the five decoys plus SRC-011 and SRC-013. Until then all seven are marked replace and are non-citable, which the publish gates enforce.

topic: Source coverage for the quality section, by topic
whyItMatters: After C.5 this is no longer one gap but a set of them, and they are in different states. Chromatography now has a modern regulatory frame around the Grant textbook; certificate content has a real source for one document type and none for the others; sterility, endotoxin, residual solvents and water have no source at all. Recording that as a single line invited the wrong conclusion in both directions — that everything was blocked, or that acquiring one document had unblocked everything.
currentSourceSignal: HELD AND EXTRACTED: SRC-006 Grant (chromatographic principles, 2002); SRC-017 ICH Q7 s.11.4 and s.17 (API and intermediate certificate content and distributor traceability). HELD, NOT YET EXTRACTED: SRC-018 ICH Q2(R2) analytical validation; SRC-019 ICH Q14 analytical procedure development; SRC-020 PDG Stage 4 harmonised <621> text, scoped as harmonised text rather than the current USP-NF chapter. REGISTERED, NO COPY HELD: SRC-021 USP <621>, SRC-022 USP <71>, SRC-023 USP <85>, SRC-024 USP <467>, SRC-025 USP <921>, SRC-026 USP <1085> — all behind a USP-NF subscription. NO SOURCE AT ALL: finished-product certificate content; third-party laboratory report conventions; certificate content for research-use material.
neededVerification: Per area. Chromatography: USP <621> to state method and system-suitability requirements (V-016). Sterility: USP <71> (V-017). Endotoxin: USP <85>, with <1085> as supporting guidance (V-018). Residual solvents: USP <467> (V-019). Water: USP <921> (V-020). Finished-product and third-party report documentation: a source of any kind, none currently identified (V-021). No area is closed until its source is registered, accessible, locator-verified and actually extracted from — holding a file is not the same as having read it.

topic: Chromatography method requirements are not established
whyItMatters: SRC-006 (Grant, 2002) supports what a chromatographic result describes and what it does not. It cannot state what a compendial method must satisfy, and this index therefore cannot say whether any particular chromatographic result was produced by an adequate method.
currentSourceSignal: SRC-020 holds the PDG Stage 4 harmonised <621> text, which is genuine but is not the current USP-NF chapter and is scoped accordingly. The official chapter (SRC-021) is behind a subscription.
neededVerification: Obtain USP <621> lawfully, audit it, and extract system-suitability and method requirements with exact locators. Until then the harmonised PDG text may be cited only as harmonised text. OWNER DECISION, 11 September 2026: a legitimate single-user USP-NF Online subscription will be obtained. Until that access exists, unauthorised copies are refused and publicly visible previews and harmonisation snippets are not treated as possession of the current chapter; the point stays an open evidence gap. On access, the chapter is ingested through the same source-integrity and locator-verification process as every other source.

topic: Certificate content is established for one document type only
whyItMatters: ICH Q7 s.11.4 states what an API or intermediate certificate should contain, and the claims drawn from it are scoped to that document type in the database. Nothing in the register states what a finished-product release document, a third-party analytical test report, or a certificate for research-use material should contain — which is most of what a reader is actually handed.
currentSourceSignal: SRC-017 (ICH Q7) held and extracted, scoped to manufacturer and repacker certificates for APIs and intermediates. No source identified for the other document types.
neededVerification: Identify and obtain a source addressing finished-product release documentation, and one addressing analytical test report conventions such as an accreditation standard. Until then the certificate reader must continue to say that these requirements are not established.

topic: Primary-source trace attempted; full text not obtainable (owner decision: do not pursue further now)
whyItMatters: Identity claims in this index rest on Grant's account of what mass spectrometry can do. Grant is a secondary source for the sequencing capability specifically, and cites two primary works for it. Neither has been obtained, so the index is relying on one author's characterisation of work it has not seen. That is an ordinary and acceptable position for a reference to be in — provided it is recorded rather than silently treated as verified.
currentSourceSignal: Grant cites Hunt, D. F., Shabanowitz, J., Yates, J. R., Griffin, P. R., and Zhu, N. Z. (1988), in Analysis of Peptides and Proteins, and Griffin, P. R., Martino, P. A., McCormack, A. L., Shabanowitz, J., and Hunt, D. F. (1990), 'Protein and oligopeptide sequence analysis on the TSQ-70 triple quadrupole mass spectrometer'. Both are chapters in edited volumes rather than journal articles. Searched 11 September 2026: no lawful free full text located for either. NOTE: Grant gives the 1988 editor as 'C. McNeil'; the volume is edited by C. J. McNeal, being the proceedings of the Fourth Texas Symposium on Mass Spectrometry (Wiley, 1988). The correction is recorded against SRC-006.
neededVerification: OWNER DECISION, 11 September 2026: do not spend further project time pursuing these chapters now. The trace stands recorded as: PRIMARY SOURCE TRACE ATTEMPTED / SOURCE IDENTIFIED / FULL TEXT NOT LAWFULLY OR RELIABLY OBTAINABLE / PRIMARY VERIFICATION NOT COMPLETED. Grant (SRC-006) remains the citable secondary academic source for the statements concerned, and the underlying claims must not be marked primary-source verified. Reopen only if library or institutional access becomes available; the bibliographic detail below is retained for exactly that purpose.
